items.title: Show HN: AgentRun: DSL to turn agents into Workflows
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN,
I just open sourced the DSL that our harness in grep.ai uses to turn repeatable parts of agent work into workflows. You can combine tool calls, code, Jev-powered system one decisions for things like routing and screening evidence, and agents when a step needs more investigation.
Our harness uses the traces and retro notes agents leave behind when doing a job to figure out which parts can become a workflow. The idea is to make the work easier to understand and avoid paying for a full agent

items.title: Show HN: Suparelay – Call any phone in the world from a browser tab
items.contentSnippet:
I'm travelling a lot, and often need to call numbers in my home country (a telco, a bank). Surprisingly, ever since Skype died, the apps that were meant to replace it launched once and never updated
So today, I'm presenting to you - Suparelay.
It works just like your phone... (revolutionary I know):
- it remembers numbers you called
- it looks like... a typical phone screen
- it has a keypad that works during the call, for those "press 1 for your account" menus
- it costs 90% less than using you

items.title: Show HN: Ceptile AI Search platform which combines web results with AI chat
items.contentSnippet:
I built Ceptile because I wanted a search tool that could combine the convenience of an AI answer with the ability to inspect the actual web pages behind it.
A Ceptile search retrieves pages from the web, ranks the retrieved sources, and uses them to produce an answer with links back to the sources. You can open the sources and continue researching from there.
I've also been building some things around the search workflow, including Notes for keeping research, translation tools, and ways to work

items.title: Show HN: I built a post-mortem debugger for native Windows x64/x86 crashes
items.contentSnippet:
Hello HN!
I've spent years debugging Windows crashes with tools that were either friendly but limited (e.g. Visual Studio) or powerful but archaic (e.g. WinDbg). I developed patterns and methods for understanding what was going on, and decided to build it into a much more effective debugging tool called ForensicDbg.

items.title: Show HN: Voyager 1 could've lasted MUCH longer
items.contentSnippet:
The reactors in Voyager 1 rely on the heat  produced by decaying plutonium, which decays  into uranium.
 We could’ve powered it with the uranium,
 But, uranium decays INCREDIBLY slowly.
 You’d have needed like, some 70,000 tons of it to power the thing,
 But, it would’ve been powered for hundreds of  thousands of years.
 Radium would’ve been the better choice.
 You’d only need about 600 pounds of it,
 And it would keep it running for thousands of years.
